narration.transcript: Want the look of old timber beams without the weight? Meet Heritage Timber by Ekena Millwork. Each beam is cast from real, weathered timber, so it looks solid, even up close. A five and a half inch beam, 12 feet long, ships at about 18 pounds. One person can lift it. It slides over a wood block with standard household tools, and it's hollow so it can hide wiring. And unlike solid wood, it resists warping and cracking with less upkeep. And here it is in real customers' homes. Pick from six hand-stained finishes or primed, eight cross-section sizes in lengths from four to 24 feet. It's in stock and usually ships in three to five business days. Order a sample and see it in your own light.

findings.rule: HOUSE_RULES.md rule 6: the edit is timed to the music's beats
findings.what: The beam and the label now change on the beat, but the swatch selector ring was not moved. Its cross-fade is centred 5-6 frames (about 90 ms) after every beat in both cuts: measured f2417.0, 2474.6, 2532.5, 2590.1, 2648.4, 2705.8 against beats 2411.7, 2468.8, 2527.4, 2584.5, 2643.0, 2700.1. These are the same values as v14. So for about 5 frames the new name and beam sit next to a ring still on the old swatch (e.g. f2414-2416: 'Kona Brown' with Sandstone ringed). This is hard to see at speed. But the v15 change note says all finish-change motion is within about 2 frames of the beat, and that isn't true for the ring.
findings.fix: render/videos/heritage-hero.mjs, 'choose' finish cycle: give the swatch ring hand-over the same beat-centred timing as the beam dissolve (start 0.175 s before the beat), or correct the change note.
